walkthroughs.body_html:
Migration to Britain c1000 to c2010 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Migration to Britain c1000 to c2010 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Migration to Britain c1000 to c2010.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What was the name of the ship arriving at Tilbury in 1948?
options: Empire Windrush
RMS Mauretania
SS Canberra
HMS Caribbean

mcqs.q: Why did Huguenots flee France in 1685?
options: French Revolution
Edict of Nantes revoked
Catholic Reformation
Napoleonic Wars

mcqs.q: How did Anglo-Saxons come to dominate post-Roman Britain?
options: Because Britain banned slavery before other countries.
Anglo-Saxons came as refugees fleeing the Vikings.
Anglo-Saxons invaded Britain and wiped out all the Romano-British inhabitants.
A mix of migration from northern Germany and Denmark, settlement and intermarriage, and cultural absorption of Romano-British populations — not simple invasion and replacement.

mcqs.q: Why did Caribbean migrants come to Britain in 1948 on the Windrush?
options: Anglo-Saxons came as refugees fleeing the Vikings.
Britain faced post-war labour shortages; the 1948 British Nationality Act gave Commonwealth citizens UK residency rights and Caribbean migrants answered the call to rebuild.
Windrush migrants came as refugees from Caribbean famines.
Windrush migrants were illegal immigrants from outside the empire.

mcqs.q: Why did the Industrial Revolution begin in Britain?
options: Because James Watt invented the steam engine.
A combination of capital from trade and empire, coal and iron deposits, agricultural improvements, political stability, and a culture of invention.
Because Britain banned slavery before other countries.
Windrush migrants came as refugees from Caribbean famines.
